elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment, including any take-or-pay commitment.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 expressly states that Customer has “no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment,” reinforced by § 12.3’s confirmation that Customer made no minimum-volume commitment.

elements.element: Customer is obligated to pay only for Services actually used or ordered.
elements.evidence: Section 2.1 limits Customer’s payment obligation to Services it “actually uses or orders under an executed Order Form.”

elements.element: If a minimum commitment applies, it is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: §§ 2.1 and 12.3 eliminate any minimum commitment, so no commitment can extend beyond the current term.

elements.element: If a minimum commitment applies, Customer may reduce it on 30 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the operative language imposes no minimum commitment requiring a reduction right.

elements.element: If Customer falls short of an applicable minimum commitment, the consequence is a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent: there is no minimum commitment or shortfall obligation, and payment is limited to Services actually used or ordered.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position by removing the three-year take-or-pay obligation and limiting payment to actual usage or executed orders. The fallback elements are satisfied only because their triggering condition—an applicable minimum commitment—is expressly absent, not because the redline includes fallback mechanics. The revision is targeted to § 2.1, leaves unrelated protections in § 12.3 intact, and introduces no contradiction.
